status: Medical only. Cannabis is dispensed by vertically integrated Medical Marijuana Treatment Centers (MMTCs) licensed by the Department of Health's Office of Medical Marijuana Use (OMMU) under s.381.986, F.S. OMMU publishes a weekly update PDF with patient counts and an operator-level dispensing table. Hemp is a separate program under FDACS: see fl-hemp.json.

facts.label: Qualified patients holding an active ID card
facts.source: Florida Department of Health, Office of Medical Marijuana Use, weekly update dated 21 August 2026, Patients section
facts.verify: 'Qualified Patients (Active ID Card): 939,639'. The weekly PDF filename encodes its date as MMDDYY; check knowthefactsmmj.com/about/weekly-updates/ for the newest before reusing this figure.

facts.label: MMTC dispensing locations statewide
facts.source: Same OMMU weekly update, MMTC Dispensations table for 14 to 20 August 2026, Total row
facts.verify: The table's own Total row reads 776. IMPORTANT: the PDF's text stream repeats the table across page renders, so a naive regex sum returns 1,466. Summing the 25 named operator rows by hand gives exactly 776, matching the Total row. Always reconcile against the printed Total.

facts.label: Share of Florida dispensing locations operated by Trulieve
facts.source: Same OMMU weekly update, MMTC Dispensations table
facts.verify: Trulieve 170 of 776 = 21.9%. Next: MUV 86, Curaleaf 75, Ayr 65, Surterra 44, Green Dragon 41. Top four operators hold 396 of 776 = 51.0%. Twenty-five MMTCs appear in the table, three of which show n/a locations and three of which show zero.

facts.label: Medical marijuana dispensed in one week, measured in milligrams of THC
facts.source: Same OMMU weekly update, MMTC Dispensations table Total row, week of 14 to 20 August 2026
facts.verify: 439,096,212 mg THC plus 1,049 mg CBD of low-THC cannabis, plus 152,157.424 ounces of marijuana in a form for smoking, in that single week. Report as dispensed volumes, never as sales dollars: OMMU publishes no revenue figure.

facts.label: Authorized dispensing locations on the state's MMTC address list
facts.source: Florida Department of Health, Office of Medical Marijuana Use, MMTC page (operator contact and dispensing location addresses)
facts.verify: 777 address rows across 23 operators, 170 cities and 48 counties. This is ONE MORE than the weekly update's 776 and the difference is fully explained: Wildflower Cannabis holds one authorized location (Jacksonville Beach) that dispensed nothing in the week of 14-20 August, so it shows 0 in the weekly dispensations table. Every other operator count matches the weekly table exactly once brand names are aligned (Sunnyside* = Sunnyside 31, GTI (Rise Dispensaries) = GTI 24, One Plant = Indiva 7, Eden Florida, LLC = Eden 4). Use 777 for authorized locations and 776 for locations that dispensed in that week, and never present them as the same measure.

facts.label: Dispensing locations in Orlando, the most of any Florida city
facts.source: Same OMMU MMTC address list, city field
facts.verify: City ranking: Orlando 43, Tampa 36, Jacksonville 35, Tallahassee 21, West Palm Beach 19, Miami 19, Pensacola 19, St. Petersburg 18, Ocala 15, Gainesville 14. County ranking: Palm Beach 56, Pinellas 54, Hillsborough 52, Orange 51, Lee 43, Duval 40, Miami-Dade 39, Broward 37. Saved as fl-locations.csv.

gaps: Sales revenue: OMMU publishes dispensed volumes (mg THC and ounces), not dollars. Do not state a Florida medical market size in dollars from this source.
Qualified physician count: the weekly update links a physician list rather than printing a total. Fetch the list page if the number is needed.
Adult use: Florida remains medical only at retrieval. Do not describe it as adult-use or predict a ballot outcome.
This file covers the OMMU cannabis programme only. Florida hemp is a separate FDACS programme with its own file (fl-hemp.json); never merge the two sets of numbers.

City counts come from the live MMTC address list and carry that day's date, while volumes come from the dated weekly PDF. The two have different currencies; never pair a city count with a weekly volume as though they describe the same moment.
